title: MEMOIR-VLM—a multimodal vision-language model for Alzheimer's disease classification and question answering
summary: On held-out ADNI subjects, the corrected encoder reported 91.3% balanced accuracy for cognitively normal versus dementia classification and 68.2% for three-class diagnosis. Zero-shot OASIS-3 evaluation reported 78.7% balanced accuracy for cognitively normal versus impaired classification (AUC 0.889) with the DTI branch masked. Subject-level held-out ADNI test set (474 subjects) and separate zero-shot OASIS-3 cohort (1,048 subjects); retrospective dataset evaluations only. The paper notes that one initial configuration leaked CDR-SB as input and reports corrected evaluation excluding it. No prospective clinical-use or outcome validation is reported.
ai_technology: A multimodal learned encoder combines MRI, diffusion imaging and clinical variables for multi-task diagnosis and regression; a retrieval-augmented language layer supports case-based question answering.
organization: Department of Neurology, University of California, San Francisco, San Francisco, California, USA
